deep.reconstruction:
PART A (end of the problem begun on p.251). The problem is to find p, q, x, y with pq(p^2-q^2) = n·xy(x^2-y^2)·(square), for a given n. Here pq(p^2-q^2) is the area of the Pythagorean triangle generated by (p, q). So the problem asks for two rational right triangles whose areas are in the ratio n times a square.

On p.251 Euler gave a parametric solution:
- p = x = s^4 - 20n s^2 t^2 - 8n^2 t^4,
- q = (s^2+2nt^2)(s^2+8nt^2),
- y = 4(s^2-nt^2)(s^2+2nt^2).

(My check.) With these values,
- q(p-q)(p+q) = -12n t^2 (s^2+2nt^2)(s^2+8nt^2)(5s^2+4nt^2)(s^2-nt^2)(s^2-4nt^2),
- y(x-y)(x+y) = -12 s^2 (the same five factors).

Since p = x, the ratio pq(p^2-q^2) / xy(x^2-y^2) = n t^2/s^2 identically. The general identity therefore holds.

On this page Euler gives examples.

(i) n=2, s=t=1. The formulas give p = 1-40-32 = -71, q = 5·17 = 85, x = -71, y = 4(-1)(5) = -20. Taking absolute values (allowed by his remark on p.251) gives p=71, q=85, x=71, y=20.
- He replaces (p, q) by its half-sum and half-difference, 78 = 2·3·13 and 7. In general p'q'(p'^2-q'^2) = pq(q^2-p^2)/4, so the square-free class is unchanged.
- Then 78·7·(78^2-7^2) = 78·7·71·85 = 2·3·5·7·13·17·71 (square-free).
- Also 71·20·(71^2-20^2) = 71·20·51·91 = 2^2·3·5·7·13·17·71. Its square-free part is 3·5·7·13·17·71, which is what Euler writes, silently dropping the factor 4.
- In fact 78·7·(78^2-7^2) = 3295110 = (1/2)·6590220 = 2·(1/2)^2·[71·20·(71^2-20^2)]. The ratio is n times a square, as required.

(ii) n=-2, s=t=1. The formulas give p = 1+40-32 = 9 and q = (-3)(-15) = 45.
- Dividing by 9 (the forms are homogeneous of degree 4) gives (1, 5). Taking half-sum and half-difference gives (3, 2).
- Likewise x = 9 and y = 4·3·(-3) = -36, which reduce to (1, 4).
- pq(p^2-q^2) = 3·2·5 = 30 = 2·3·5.
- |xy(x^2-y^2)| = 4·15 = 60, with square-free part 3·5.
- So 30 = 2·15. The sign of n is absorbed by interchanging x and y.
- In triangle terms: the triangles (5, 12, 13) and (8, 15, 17) have areas 30 and 60.

Source: A. m. T. III p.121-123.

PART B, No. 70 (W. L. Krafft). Problem: x+y+z = square, xyz = 1, so z = 1/(xy). Six particular solutions are listed (all verified by me):
- I. (1/2, 9/2, 4/9): sum 49/9 = (7/3)^2.
- II. (2/9, 50/9, 81/100): sum 5929/900 = (77/30)^2.
- III. (13/392, 117/392, 392^2/(9·13^2)): sum 30217009/298116 = (5497/546)^2.
- IV. (2/5, 18/5, 25/36): sum 169/36 = (13/6)^2.
- V. (-2, -2/9, 9/4): sum 1/36 = (1/6)^2.
- VI. (1/6, 1/12, 72): sum 289/4 = (17/2)^2.

All six have product 1.

Method: fix the ratio x:y = a:b and put x = ma, y = mb, so z = 1/(m^2 ab).
- The condition is m(a+b) + 1/(m^2 ab) = square.
- Multiplying by the square m^2 gives m^3(a+b) + 1/(ab) = square.
- Multiplying by a^2 b^2 gives m^3 a^2 b^2 (a+b) + ab = square.
- For fixed a, b this is a plane cubic (an elliptic curve) in (m, w).

(My observation.) Solutions I, III and IV all have a:b = 1:9. The equation then reduces to 90m^3 + 1 = square, with m = 1/2, 2/5, 13/392:
- m = 1/2 gives 49/4.
- m = 2/5 gives 169/25.
- m = 13/392: rescaling 90m^3+1 by the square (392/39)^2 gives exactly the sum in III, which is a square.

So these are several rational points on one elliptic curve. II has a:b = 1:25, V has 9:1, VI has 2:1.

Source: A. m. T. I p.121.

PART C, No. 71 (Lexell). Concordant forms: make a^2 + M b^2 and a^2 + N b^2 both squares.
- Rule: write M = mμ and take N = (αp^2+m)(αq^2+μ).
- (Implicit, supplied from the next page.) Take a = μp^2 - mq^2 and b = 2pq. Then a^2 + Mb^2 = (μp^2+mq^2)^2 and a^2 + Nb^2 = (μp^2 - mq^2 + 2αp^2q^2 + 2m q^2)^2.
- Hence, for given M, there are infinitely many admissible N.

Special case M = 1, m = μ = ±1: N = (αp^2±1)(αq^2±1). For p = 1: N = (α±1)(αq^2±1). Listed:
- α=1: N = 2(q^2+1).
- α=2: N = 3(2q^2+1) or 2q^2-1.
- α=3: N = 4(3q^2+1) or 2(3q^2-1).
- α=4: N = 5(4q^2+1) or 3(4q^2-1).

Example (mine): α=2, q=2 gives N=27. With a=-3, b=4: 9+16 = 25 and 9+27·16 = 441 = 21^2.
errors: No genuine errors on this page.
Euler writes xy(xx-yy)=3.5.7.13.17.71 with '='. Strictly 71·20·(71^2-20^2) = 2^2·3·5·7·13·17·71. He means equality up to square factors (square-free kernel).

Signs are suppressed throughout: the formulas give p=x=-71, y=-20 for n=2 and y=-36 for n=-2. xy(xx-yy) for (1,4) is -60. Euler explicitly allowed taking absolute values on p.251, and swapping x,y absorbs the sign of n, so this is legitimate.

(Previous page, relevant here.) The stated factorizations p-q=6ntt(5ss+4ntt) and x-y=3ss(ss+8ntt) are off by a sign. Actually p-q = -6nt^2(5s^2+4nt^2) and x-y = -3s^2(s^2+8nt^2). This is harmless, since only absolute values matter.

In No. 71 the letter α (alpha) is a new free parameter, distinct from the a in aa+Mbb. The accompanying values of a, b (a=μpp-mqq, b=2pq) are not stated on this page; they appear in the next fragment.

results.what: Parametric solution of pq(p^2-q^2) = n·xy(x^2-y^2)·□ (two Pythagorean triangles with area ratio n·square), with numerical examples n=±2: triangles from (78,7)&(71,20) and (3,2)&(4,1)
results.modern_name: Congruent-number-type problem: rational points relating the twists y^2=x^3-x and ny^2=x^3-x (areas of rational right triangles in a given square class)
results.usually_credited_to: Diophantine tradition (Fibonacci, Fermat, Frenicle); Euler worked extensively on such area problems

results.what: Six rational solutions of x+y+z=□, xyz=1, and reduction to m^3 a^2 b^2 (a+b) + ab = □
results.modern_name: Rational points on an elliptic curve (cubic in m) via chord-tangent/trial; the family x+y+z = w^2, xyz = 1

results.what: Given M=mμ, N=(αp^2+m)(αq^2+μ) makes a^2+Mb^2 and a^2+Nb^2 simultaneously squares (a=μp^2-mq^2, b=2pq); tables for M=1
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (E718 'De binis formulis speciei xx+myy et xx+nyy inter se concordibus et discordibus', and related papers)

deep.surprise_reason: Worked numerical examples and routine Diophantine notes (areas of Pythagorean triangles, x+y+z=□ with xyz=1, concordant forms) are all well within Euler's known published work on these topics.

checkable.asserts: Lexell's rule makes a^2+N b^2 a square

transcription_corrections: In No. 71 the parameter in N=(αpp+m)(αqq+μ) and in 'pro α=1, α=2,...' is the Greek letter α, not a. The transcription mixes 'app', 'aqq' with 'α=1'. It should read N=(αpp+m)(αqq+μ), N=(αpp±1)(αqq±1), N=(α±1)(αqq±1).
Otherwise the transcription matches the image (e.g. q=5.9, y=4.9, z=392^2/(9.13^2) are correct).
